name: Man Parrish
hook: Built a club-floor anthem almost entirely out of a drum machine and two synthesizers, months ahead of 'Planet Rock' making that the whole point.

blurb.age7: He made a famous dance song using mostly a drum machine and two keyboards, without much singing.
blurb.age13: Parrish grew up in Brooklyn on funk and experimental electronic music, then built 'Hip Hop, Be Bop (Don't Stop)' in 1982 almost entirely from a Roland TR-808 and a couple of synthesizers, with barely any vocal. It came out before 'Planet Rock' and is one of electro's very first records.
blurb.adult: 'Hip Hop, Be Bop' is a useful counterweight to 'Planet Rock' as electro's origin point: a record built from the same machine, arriving from downtown New York's club and disco underground rather than from the Bronx sound-system lineage, on almost exactly the same timeline. Genre origin stories rarely have one clean start, and this is a clean case of two.

signatureTracks.title: Hip Hop, Be Bop (Don't Stop)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Built almost entirely from a TR-808 and synthesizers with minimal vocal, and among the earliest records to put the 808 at the center rather than in the background.

signatureTracks.title: Male Stripper
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A club record that found a second life on UK charts nearly a decade later, showing how far electro's reach outlasted its founding scene.
